rules.title: M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B (limits on upfront charges by lessors)
rules.requirement: Before a tenancy begins, a lessor may require payment only of first month's rent, last month's rent, a security deposit and a lock-change fee. Application, pet, cleaning, amenity and other fees are forbidden for landlords.
rules.key_value: Only first, last, security deposit and lock change may be charged upfront
rules.penalty: Federal court in Perry v. Equity Residential awarded tenants treble damages and attorney's fees
rules.status_basis: Described as existing law in effect since the 1970s.

requires.name: lessor_bound
requires.text: applies to lessors; licensed brokers are treated separately

coverage.summary: Applies to landlords (lessors) of residential tenancies.

rules.quoted_span: It states that prior to the beginning of a tenancy, no lessor may require payment for anything except first, last, security, and locks ( MGL Ch 186 Section 15B ).

rules.title: 254 CMR 7 (broker regulations on fees to prospective tenants)
rules.requirement: Licensed brokers may charge fees to prospective tenants if they give written notice of the fee amount, time and manner of payment, and whether it is contingent on a lease. The notice must be given at the first personal meeting and signed by the applicant, with any refusal recorded.
rules.status_basis: Described as existing board of registration regulations.

requires.name: broker_bound
requires.text: applies to licensed brokers or salesmen, not landlords

coverage.summary: Applies to licensed brokers dealing with prospective tenants.

rules.quoted_span: In addition to holding a valid license, the broker has to tell the applicant in writing the amount of the broker’s fee, the time and manner of payment, and whether it is contingent on the owner and applicant actually entering into a lease or rental agreement.
